task: Harden MLX orphan marker ownership and process identity, and reconcile MLX state after system sleep/wake

events.summary: Backend MLX lifecycle only: owner and start-time marker identity, wake heartbeat and Rust IPC documentation. No frontend, health, RAG, airgap, support-bundle, hardware soak, or live process termination work.

Regression cases cover another live app owner retaining its marker, process start-time mismatch refusing identity, whitespace in a venv path, and injected wall-clock progress diverging from monotonic progress. The live-owner test also requires no malformed-marker report.

New markers record MLX PID, owning app PID, and sysinfo process start time. Scans skip markers owned by another live app, reject start-time mismatches, and refuse termination for legacy PID-only markers. SIGTERM and SIGKILL paths compare process start time; training falls back to the PID when no process group exists. A wall/monotonic heartbeat marks training and serving slots separately for re-verification, rescans MLX markers, and emits mlx-lifecycle-wake. The next status request verifies training's MLX command line and serving's /v1/models health before clearing each flag.
Lifecycle regressions and fake-clock wake detector tests passed.
